ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, and beneficial owners against the Luxembourg CSSF consolidated list, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, and the national list of politically exposed persons (PEPs) maintained by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered if any individual or entity is identified as a PEP, is connected to a jurisdiction on the FATF grey/black list, or operates in a high-risk industry sector. EDD requires corroboration of funds origin, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. For equity crowdfunding platforms, a risk-based assessment must also capture the AML/CFT risk of each underlying project promoter, each major investor (above the 25% threshold), and the payment intermediaries involved in the escrow chain. The platform operator must establish a transaction monitoring program adapted to the scale of retail investor flows, including sanctions list screening in real-time at onboarding and on an ongoing basis before each funding round settlement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a Luxembourg SARL may be in French, German, or any other language using the Latin script; if a non-Latin language is used, a transliteration into the Latin alphabet is mandatory for RCS registration. All corporate documents must include the name alongside the legal form designation 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. The name must be freely available within the RCS and must not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights or existing Luxembourg trademarks. The name must not be contrary to public order or morality.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the RCS, the applicant is entitled to resubmit an amended name application without prejudice, but for an administrative appeal against a formal refusal, the applicant must address a written remonstrance (recours gracieux) to the Registrar of the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of the notification of refusal, detailing the legal basis for the admissibility of the proposed name. If the recours gracieux is denied, a formal appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg administrative tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months from the date of the decision. In urgent cases, an interim stay can be requested before the President of the Administrative Tribunal. The appeal will be governed by the provisions of the amended law on the organization of the RCS and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 November 2022 on business registers.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office (non-residential address without any physical presence) is generally permissible for a standard Luxembourg SARL for general corporate purposes, but for a regulated equity crowdfunding portal under CSSF supervision, the practice is discouraged and the CSSF will require a genuine physical presence in Luxembourg, including available administrative staff and equipment. A 'domiciliation' arrangement with a registered office service provider is tolerated solely for the incorporation stage and only where the actual substance, including at least one local manager or effective director, is in Luxembourg. The CSSF will verify that the platform has a stable local establishment, maintains personnel proportionate to the scale of activities, and is able to produce all necessary records immediately upon request.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% — For a crowdfunding portal authorized by the CSSF, the probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months of operation is high, and the platform must be prepared for a full audit including the review of client files for AML/KYC compliance, source of funds documentation, and the adequacy of internal risk management procedures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (consolidated by the Law of 10 August 2016 modernising company law), Articles 710-1 to 710-20 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); supplemented by Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 on European Crowdfunding Service Providers and the amended Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector for the operational crowdfunding licence.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), attached to the Luxembourg District Court
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation containing the Articles of Association (Statuts), filed with the RCS and published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 for a SARL, fully subscribed and fully paid up in cash or in kind at incorporation; the funds must be held in a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company 'en formation' and are released only upon issuance of the RCS registration certificate; no separate state escrow account is required. For the equity crowdfunding licence, the CSSF prudential own-funds requirement is at least EUR 25,000 or one tenth of fixed overheads (or 25% of forecast fixed overheads for the year following authorisation), whichever is higher.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED FIRST: that the draft Articles of Association dated [date] are approved, and the incorporation deed shall be passed before a Luxembourg notary. RESOLVED SECOND: that the subscription of the EUR 12,000 share capital by the founders is ratified, and the manager is instructed to maintain the blocked capital account until RCS registration. RESOLVED THIRD: that the registered office is fixed at [address], Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg, where the statutory registers shall be kept. RESOLVED FOURTH: that [Name] is appointed Manager (Gérant) with full power of representation, and [Firm] is appointed Réviseur d'entreprises agréé. RESOLVED FIFTH: that the Manager is authorised to complete the RCS filing, the CSSF ECSP application and all ancillary declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Negative Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - online filing channel MyGuichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit at least five proposed company names, each including the legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL', through the MyGuichet.lu portal. The LBR verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name is already registered and issues a 'certificat de non-confusion' (negative certificate), which has a limited statutory validity and must be referenced in the notarial deed.
required_dossiers: MyGuichet electronic application form
List of five proposed names with suffix 'SARL'
Identity document of the applicant or founder
Optional trademark search confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR refuses the name on grounds of confusing similarity, re-file an amended set of name proposals without any additional fee; if the applicant disputes the refusal, a formal objection may be lodged with the administrative department of the LBR within one month of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Blocked Capital Account (Compte Bloqué)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, Spuerkees, Banque de Luxembourg) supervised by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company 'en formation' and deposit the full EUR 12,000. Each founder signs a subscription commitment; the bank performs standard KYC and source-of-funds checks and issues a blocked-funds attestation to be presented to the notary at the signing of the deed. The funds are released automatically upon production of the RCS registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association
Share subscription list with subscriber signatures
Passport or national identity card of each subscriber
Proof of address dated within the last three months
Source of funds declaration and bank statements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML queries, provide notarised wealth statements, bank references and a corporate structure explanation; if the account is refused, engage an alternate Luxembourg credit institution or a professional of the financial sector (PCI). Re-present the revised KYC package within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (member of the Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary finalises the Statuts, verifies the negative certificate and the blocked-capital attestation, checks the legality and capacity of the founders, and authenticates the deed of incorporation. In the case of a sole founder, the deed is a unilateral act; with multiple founders, all must appear in person or by notarised power of attorney. The deed is drafted in French or German and is authenticated by the notary, who then triggers electronic filing with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Negative certificate (certificat de non-confusion)
Bank blocked-funds attestation
Founders' identity documents
Draft Articles of Association
Declaration of non-insolvency of founders and managers
Power of attorney if any founder is not present in person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies irregularities in the draft deed, issue an amendatory rider (acte rectificatif) signed by the founders before the same notary; any contribution in kind must be revalued by an independent réviseur d'entreprises as required by law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the notarial deed, the LBR examines its conformity, allocates the registration number and issues the certificate of registration (extrait du RCS). The legal existence of the SARL commences on the date of registration. The LBR simultaneously publishes the extract in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations), completing the publicity requirement effective against third parties.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed of incorporation transmitted by the notary
Full text of the Articles of Association
Extract of the deed specifying statutory particulars
Payment receipt of the LBR filing fee (approx. EUR 75)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR issues a regularity query, submit a corrective deed within fifteen days; if registration is refused on legal substance grounds, amend the defective clause and re-notarise the deed, or appeal the refusal in writing to the District Court registry within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); LBR Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online for the Luxembourg VAT number via MyGuichet within fifteen days of registration (form 1609/1610); register as an employer with the CCSS for social security affiliation of the manager and employees; file the beneficial ownership declaration with the RBE within one month of incorporation; obtain an EORI number if the platform will onboard international enterprises; notify the communal tax authority of the registered office for local business tax purposes.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait du RCS)
VAT application form 1609/1610
Manager's identification and social security number
Beneficial owners' identity details for the RBE
Bank account details (IBAN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of late filings, submit a spontaneous declaration (déclaration tardive) with an explanatory letter to the AEDT to mitigate flat-rate penalties; any penalty may be challenged by a written request for remission (demande de remise gracieuse) within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CSSF European Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP) Authorisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) - Prudential Supervision and Innovation & Payments Departments, via the CSSF eDesk portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the complete ECSP application under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 and CSSF Circular 21/788. The application must include the programme of operations, a three-year business plan, governance and anti-money laundering/CTF policies under the amended Law of 12 November 2004, own-funds evidence of at least EUR 25,000 or one tenth of fixed overheads (25% of forecast overheads for the first year after authorisation), whichever is higher, IT security and outsourced hosting arrangements, and fit-and-proper documentation of senior managers. The CSSF assesses the file within three months of completeness and notifies ESMA after a positive decision.
required_dossiers: CSSF ECSP application questionnaire
Programme of operations and organisational chart
Three-year business plan and financial projections
Capital and own-funds attestation from the depository bank
AML/CTF policy and investor-complaint procedure
IT security policy, business continuity plan and hosting agreement
Curricula vitae, criminal record extracts and declarations of honour of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSSF issues a deficiency letter (lettre de carence), respond with detailed clarifications within the stated deadline, generally thirty days; if the authorisation is refused, cure the identified gaps and re-file, or appeal the decision before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal Administratif) within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) - Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission, in coordination with the Administration de l'environnement for premises-related permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: European Crowdfunding Service Provider (ECSP) Authorisation under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 and CSSF Circular 21/788, covering the operation of a digital equity crowdfunding portal, reception and transmission of funding orders, and handling of payment and escrow flows

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Registration only; no full EIA report required because the activity is a digital intermediary with an office-only footprint; premises must be registered for commercial waste management and must hold an energy performance certificate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions since no manufacturing is performed; compliance with Directive 2012/19/EU (WEEE) for disposal of IT servers, UPS batteries and electronic equipment through registered waste collectors; compliance with the amended Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management for segregation and documented disposal of non-hazardous commercial waste; noise emissions of HVAC equipment and backup generators limited to 40 dB(A) at night where the office is located in a mixed residential-commercial zone.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety authorisation delivered by the communal fire prevention service (Service de prévention incendie) covering evacuation plans, smoke detection, fire extinguishers and emergency lighting; structural load verification by a certified engineer for the server room and archive areas; occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering conformity of electrical installations, safe workstations, first-aid equipment and management of psychosocial risks; certificate of maximum occupation density and accessibility for the premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; Administration des douanes et accises for customs; unified taxpayer portal: MyGuichet.lu / espace securise (guichet.lu) operated with the Government IT Center (CTIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The SARL is incorporated by a Luxembourg notary and filed with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), which issues the company's RCS registration number. Step 2: The ACD automatically allocates the corporate taxpayer identification number (matricule d'identification) upon extraction from the RCS file; non-resident entities without an RCS file must apply by filing the first corporate income tax and net wealth tax return. Step 3: VAT registration is submitted electronically on MyGuichet.lu using the matricule; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits) within approximately two weeks. A non-resident crowdfunding portal supplying taxable services in Luxembourg must appoint a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative and file via the eCDF module. Step 4: The CSSF crowdfunding licence under the Law of 16 July 2019 and Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (ECSPR) must be granted before client onboarding; the regulatory licence creates an unconditional VAT registration obligation regardless of the EUR 30,000 small-business franchise.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Luxembourg SARL (Societe a Responsabilite Limitee) is an opaque corporate person fully tax resident in Luxembourg where its registered office or place of effective management is in Luxembourg; it is subject to entity-level corporate income tax (IRC) at 17%, a 7% solidarity surcharge (aggregate 18.19%), municipal business tax (impot commercial communal, e.g., 6.75% in Luxembourg City, making an aggregate headline rate of approximately 24.94%), and net wealth tax (0.5% on taxable net wealth); no territorial scope limitation, no pass-through election exists; the entity is not situated in a tax-exempt zone; the equity-crowdfunding activity is a licensed financial-sector activity subject to CSSF supervision.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. Relevant elections include: (i) fiscal unity (integration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR, available to a resident parent holding at least 95% direct or indirect ownership in resident subsidiaries for a five-year commitment period; (ii) participation exemption election for qualifying shareholdings (minimum 10% capital participation or an acquisition cost of at least EUR 1.2 million) held for at least 12 months, exempting dividends and capital gains under Articles 147, 148 and 166 LIR; (iii) hybrid mismatch elections and counter-measures under ATAD rules implemented in Articles 168quater to 168septies LIR; (iv) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) election under Article 21 of the VAT Law for closely-linked financial entities; (v) no election permits pass-through treatment for the SARL because the CSSF licence requires a regulated, taxable legal vehicle; (vi) optional application of notional interest deduction under Article 168bis LIR in the ordinary CIT return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / TVA (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutee) governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (as amended), transposing EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 on annual taxable turnover for the small-business exemption scheme (Article 177 of the VAT Law). The threshold is unavailable to a CSSF-licenced crowdfunding service provider because licensed financial activities are mandatorily registrable irrespective of turnover; a non-established foreign portal supplying Luxembourg B2B services must register under the non-established taxable person / EU One Stop Shop (OSS) procedure and cannot invoke the EUR 30,000 franchise.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time national fiscal clearance or mandatory continuous transaction-control mandate (unlike the Italian SDI model). Electronic invoicing is mandatory for B2G supplies to Luxembourg public-sector authorities through the PEPPOL network in PEPPOL BIS 3.0 / EN 16931 format; private B2B e-invoicing is permitted in any EU-standard XML or PDF format. All VAT returns (Model 1026 TVA), recapitulative EC Sales Lists and Intrastat declarations must be filed electronically via the AEDT's eCDF central filing module on MyGuichet.lu; invoices must display the LU VAT number of the supplier and the customer; the crowdfunding portal's escrow, ACH and bank-wire payment rails must preserve an immutable documentary audit trail for AEDT inspection for at least 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% VAT applies when goods are dispatched or transported by the supplier to a non-EU destination, evidenced by EU customs export clearance; intra-EU B2B supplies are zero-rated when the customer provides a valid EU VAT identification number and the goods are transported to another Member State. Services: B2B platform, escrow, custody, administrative and due-diligence services supplied by the portal to a business customer established outside Luxembourg fall outside the Luxembourg place-of-supply under the general B2B rule and are reportable as zero-rated/outside scope; B2C remote digital intermediary services supplied to EU consumers are taxable via the OSS scheme in the consumer's Member State; services effectively rendered offshore and invoiced to non-EU business counterparties evidenced by a valid non-EU VAT/tax registration certificate qualify for 0%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD - Single Administrative Document) electronically lodged through the Luxembourg AES/ECS export system
Bill of Lading (maritime), Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure from Luxembourg/EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or authenticated bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU counterparty
Commercial export invoice with Incoterms and declared customs value
Proof of export status: customs office exit stamp or electronic ARN/EX number from the AES/ECS export clearance record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or improperly substantiated export zero-rating is sanctioned under Articles 427-433 of the General Tax Law and Article 59 of the VAT Law. The AEDT may reassess uncollected VAT at 17% on the full consideration for up to 5 years (10 years in cases of wilful tax fraud), impose default interest at 0.6% per month, and levy administrative fines of 10%-25% of the evaded tax, rising to 100% for deliberate concealment. Criminal tax fraud is punishable with imprisonment of one to five years and fines up to EUR 150,000; the VAT representative and managing officers incur joint and several liability. For regulated crowdfunding portals, cross-border export or disbursement anomalies are flagged through the Eurofisc network, with retroactive clawback of refunded export VAT and suspension of zero-rating privileges for at least 24 months.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as the national central bank within the Eurosystem and responsible for Luxembourg's balance-of-payments statistics, TARGET2 participation, currency circulation, and oversight of payment systems. The Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the competent financial-sector supervisor for the licensed equity crowdfunding service provider, including AML/CFT supervision, licensing, and prudential controls over banking and payment operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the euro as sole legal tender and operates a fully liberalised current and capital account regime under Articles 63 to 66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There is no exchange-control statute, no central bank approval requirement for inward or outward capital movements, and no distinction between current-account and capital-account convertibility in domestic law. Profit remittance is unrestricted at the FX level; the only material hurdle is the Luxembourg withholding tax of 15% on dividends distributed by an SARL, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU corporate shareholders under Directive 2011/96/EU and further relieved under applicable double tax treaties. Distributions are legally blocked where they would cause the company's net assets to fall below the called-up share capital plus the non-distributable statutory reserve, which is set at 5% of annual net profits until reaching 5% of subscribed share capital. For the equity crowdfunding portal, investor funds are not corporate assets: the platform must hold all client monies in segregated escrow compartments at a credit institution, ring-fenced from the platform's insolvency estate, and such funds may only be released to the relevant issuer or refunded to investors in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 and the Luxembourg law of 18 July 2016 on crowdfunding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender obligation exists in Luxembourg or elsewhere in the euro area. The statutory conversion ratio for export receipts is zero percent and no mandatory timeline applies; a Luxembourg resident company may lawfully retain foreign currency proceeds in any currency and jurisdiction, subject only to general anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and transfer-pricing rules. The only administrative requirement is indirect: resident credit institutions and, where directly relevant, resident enterprises must report cross-border flows to the BCL under EU Regulation 184/2005 and BCL implementing instructions, using the applicable balance-of-payments purpose codes for direct investment, loans, and other services.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) / Spuerkeess

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High, subject to strict structural limits. An EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institution or Payment Institution may be onboarded under the PSD2 passport into Luxembourg as a technical payment gateway for collecting and disbursing investor funds, provided the EMI has completed the CSSF notification procedure and holds adequate safeguarding arrangements. Regulation (EU) 2020/1503, Article 10, however, requires the crowdfunding service provider itself to ensure that client funds are protected in the event of the platform's insolvency, which in practice compels holding the pooled investor monies at a supervised credit institution or at an EMI that holds such funds in a segregated account. Luxembourg banks will typically permit the EMI as an execution-only routing layer but will require the platform's own escrow ledger to remain with the credit institution opening the relationship. Non-EEA offshore digital EMIs without a Luxembourg or European passport are not viable for investor-facing operations, as receiving funds from Luxembourg residents without local licensing would constitute an unauthorised payment service under CSSF enforcement practice.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legally permitted route allows remote onboarding where the bank applies tamper-resistant identification and a live video interview authenticated by an eIDAS-qualified electronic signature, consistent with the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02. However, for a High_Risk_Special_License crowdfunding portal, the de facto market standard is that at least one natural-person director and the ultimate beneficial owner must appear physically at the bank's Luxembourg premises, or before a Luxembourg notary or consular officer acting under an apostilled power of attorney, before the account is activated. The recommended practical protocol is to schedule one physical meeting in Luxembourg for the CEO or principal UBO, accompanied by the corporate books, notarised articles, RCS extract, RBE certificate, and the CSSF/ECSPR authorisation file; second signatories may be onboarded remotely through a strengthened video verification route at the bank's discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The crowdfunding platform cannot prove that it is actually supervised as a financial-sector entity or that the SARL holds the required authorisation to operate an equity crowdfunding portal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the authorisation granted by the CSSF under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 or under the Luxembourg law of 18 July 2016 on crowdfunding; proof of European passport notification for any target Member State; current Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCSL) extract; notarised articles of association; criminal record extracts for each director and UBO; the firm's AML/CFT policy and risk assessment evidencing compliance with CSSF Regulation 12-02.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the ultimate beneficial ownership chain, in particular intermediate holding vehicles holding 25% or more, or any nominee-like arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date certificate of registration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), complete share register, signed organisational chart, source of wealth declaration from each UBO, and bank or notary references covering the origin of the initial equity capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media findings on founders, key investors, or issuer companies in the crowdfunding portfolio.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Real-time screening output against the EU consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council listings, and OFAC; PEP questionnaire and status declaration; enhanced due diligence files for all foreign investors in the escrow verification wall; documentary evidence of a clean regulatory history from the CSSF for the platform and its issuer counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Portfolio inflows routed through crypto-asset wallets, unexplained third-party payment aggregators, or mixed-purpose wires that obscure the investor/reference matching requirement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed representation that all investor funds arrive exclusively through bank wire (SEPA or SWIFT MT103) and approved ACH escrow rails; confirmation that the platform performs no crypto-asset custody or exchange function; transaction-matching documentation proving that each escrow credit corresponds to an investor reservation ticket; technical evidence that the settlement architecture contains no tokenised exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection into the SARL originates from loans or intra-group advances rather than clear share subscription, creating doubt about the solvency and independent standing of the platform.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised shareholders resolution approving the capital increase; proof of payment by MT103 or SEPA credit transfer referencing the share subscription purpose; bank-to-bank value confirmation; an accounting file audited by a Luxembourg statutory auditor mapping the receipt to the share capital account; shareholder loan agreement with market terms where related-party funding is complementary.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity subscriptions into the Luxembourg SARL are executed by SWIFT MT103 for USD/GBP and other non-euro currencies, and by SEPA Credit Transfer for euro amounts; high-value euro transfers settle in central bank money on TARGET2 (T2 RTGS) with the BCL as the national settlement agent. The beneficiary bank verifies the name-match against the RCSL, checks the wire for the correct balance-of-payments purpose code, and applies sanctions and AML screening to the remitter. For a share capital injection the remittance reference should identify that the payment is a subscription for shares; for shareholder loans the reference should identify the intercompany credit. Where the historical funding route is US ACH escrow, the US leg clears through an approved partner institution and the cross-border leg reaches Luxembourg as a SWIFT MT103 with an unambiguous beneficiary reference. For crowdfunding investor funds, the inbound escrow process requires every receipt to carry a unique investor reference, enabling automatic reconciliation against the platform ledger; the Luxembourg financial intelligence unit (Cellule de Renseignements Financiers) receives reports for suspicious operations exceeding EUR 10,000, and the platform must retain the source-of-funds and beneficial-ownership evidence for each investor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Euro-denominated outbound disbursements, including issuer payouts, refunds, and operating expenses, clear through SEPA Credit Transfer in ISO 20022 format or through SEPA Instant for near-real-time obligations. Cross-border payments in foreign currency are routed by SWIFT MT103 with strict reference matching; disbursements to US beneficiaries may settle on the domestic US leg via ACH or Fedwire through a partner bank before the euro leg is delivered to the Luxembourg treasury. Where the underlying investment involves documentary trade finance, the commercial bank's trade desk issues Letters of Credit under UCP 600 or handles Collections under URC 522, with euro settlement through the T2 correspondent network. The platform's escrow system must maintain a closed loop: no client money can leave the segregated compartment until the target closing conditions under ECSPR are met, and each outgoing instruction must carry the corresponding investor reservation ticket, the issuer closing record, and the final cap-table update.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright forwards aligned with the underlying issuance and disbursement cycle
FX swaps for rolling settlement liquidity without extending residual currency exposure
Mark-to-market cross-currency swaps for long-dated foreign-currency assets associated with acquired SPV positions

Purchased long-dated FX option strategies protecting committed capital subscription obligations; writing naked or uncovered FX options is not permitted under Luxembourg prudential practice for a non-bank treasury

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (higher corporate income tax bracket above EUR 200,000), plus 7% solidarity surcharge levied on the CIT, plus municipal business tax at approximately 6.75% in Luxembourg City; combined statutory headline rate ≈ 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% CIT rate on the first EUR 200,000 of taxable income; 100% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains (≥10% holding held for 12 months); IP box regime granting an 80% exemption on net qualified IP income (effective rate circa 5%); 8% investment tax credit for eligible capex; 25% taxable base reduction for young innovative companies; minimum net wealth tax rules overridden by solidarity surcharge offset arrangements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return - IRC), filed jointly with Formulaire 200 (Municipal Business Tax - ICC) and Formulaire 500 (Net Wealth Tax - IFT); mandatory electronic filing via the MyGuichet.lu / e-Tax portal (FDL XML dataset, SIP integrated system) of the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline: 31 March following the fiscal year-end; administratively extended to 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end (e.g., FY 31 December 2024 return due 31 December 2025); quarterly advance CIT/ICC instalments are due in February, May, August and November of the current tax year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State the Luxembourg national business identifier (RCS registration number and LIGI matricule), legal form (SARL), registered office address, and the statutory license number of the equity crowdfunding portal issued under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (ECSPR).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable to the resident SARL; non-resident shareholders and beneficial owners must be disclosed on Schedule RBE (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) and to the CSSF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box B - Profit and Loss Account (State B)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report certified annual accounts prepared under LUX GAAP; include all crowdfunding platform fee income, escrow administration fees, success fees, and ancillary intermediation revenues under ISIC 6499 as taxable trading income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities without a Luxembourg permanent establishment must not be included in Box B; cross-border crowdfunding services may create a Luxembourg taxable presence where staff or physical infrastructure are maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Re-add non-deductible expenditures: 50% of client entertainment costs, corporate income tax and solidarity surcharge, municipal business tax, late-payment interest, fines, and any expenses benefiting persons other than the company without valid consideration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany payments to non-resident related parties must be justified by arm's length agreements; failing that, amounts are reintegrated and potentially 15% dividend withholding tax is triggered on constructive distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare qualifying dividend and capital gain income relieved under Article 166 LIR (participation exemption) where the SARL holds ≥10% participation held for at least 12 months and the subsidiary is subject to comparable taxation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach foreign tax residence certificates and substantiate the 12-month holding period; non-resident ultimate shareholders are irrelevant to this claim but must satisfy substance conditions if treaty benefits are sought.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim the 80% exemption on net qualifying intellectual property income under Article 50bis LIR for software patents, algorithms, or portal technology developed within the Luxembourg establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only income derived from qualifying IP assets owned and economically exploited in Luxembourg qualifies; acquisition from related non-resident parties triggers commensurate arm's length valuations and nexus-labour expenditure documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset available net operating losses previously assessed against current-year taxable income within the 17-year carryforward period under Article 110 LIR; no carryback is permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of non-resident shareholders cannot be transferred to the Luxembourg SARL; a Luxembourg permanent establishment of a non-resident may offset only losses attributable to that establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E - Municipal Business Tax Schedule (ICC)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the ICC base using the communal trade multiplier of the municipality of the registered office; standard Luxembourg City multiplier yields an effective rate of 6.75% on adjusted profits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident persons are not subject to ICC unless operating through a Luxembourg permanent establishment; flat-rate attribution rules apply to intermediation activities conducted from Luxembourg premises.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box F - Net Wealth Tax and Solidarity Surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the 7% employment fund solidarity surcharge on the assessed CIT; declare net wealth tax at 0.5% on net taxable wealth exceeding EUR 500,000 after deductible allowances; minimum IFT charges apply for holdings companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders holding crowdfunding platform equity are not subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax; portfolio assets managed in Luxembourg escrow accounts remain taxable assets of the SARL only.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 100/200/500 triggers procedural fines up to EUR 25,000 and imposition d'office (automatic contested assessment), loss of partial deductions and reliefs, default interest at 0.8% per commenced month on all unpaid taxes, and a late payment surcharge of 10% on the outstanding liability; unremedied filing of annual accounts with the RCS adds civil fines up to EUR 5,000 per missing filing.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on distributions (LIR Art. 105 and 115); reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate shareholder holds a participation of at least 10% for an uninterrupted 12-month period; applicable treaty rates range from 0% to 15%, with the 0% rate commonly available for EU/EEA parent companies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Protocol: (1) the non-resident corporate shareholder obtains an official tax residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale) from its home tax administration; (2) the certificate and a beneficial-ownership declaration are delivered to the Luxembourg SARL before the dividend record date; (3) the SARL applies the reduced of zero WHT at source after verifying substance and beneficial ownership under Circular LIR 168 and the anti-abuse/GAAR provisions; (4) if excess WHT was withheld, the non-resident applies to the ACD for refund within the statutory assessment window; (5) a current tax clearance certificate from the Luxembourg tax office may be required before final distribution is executed for large dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: no domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound interest payments (0%); royalties: no domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound royalty payments (0%); the EU Interest & Royalties Directive provides full relief for qualifying associated enterprises in other Member States; bilateral treaty rates for interest typically fall between 0% and 10% and for royalties between 0% and 5%, but domestic statutory exemption renders the treaty relief largely redundant for pure interest and royalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: EUR 100,000 in aggregate controlled transactions for any single related-party transaction category (loan, service, licensing, financing) under the Luxembourg transfer pricing documentation law of 28 December 2023, applicable to tax years commencing on or after 1 January 2023; Master File: mandatory where the consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 750,000,000; Country-by-Country Report (DAC4/CbCR): required for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000, filed with the ACD and exchanged automatically.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply offshore Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as such, but substantive presence is indirectly mandated through: (i) the ATAD GAAR and CFC rules, (ii) the participation exemption substance test under Article 148/166 LIR, (iii) Administrative Circular LIR 14/4 requiring real local value-adding functions for tax residence and treaty access, and (iv) the beneficial ownership thresholds applied to WHT reductions; a licensed equity crowdfunding portal under ECSPR must retain licensed registered offices in Luxembourg, qualified AML/CFT responsible officers, locally employed transaction and compliance staff, board minutes evidencing Luxembourg decision-making, and operational bank/escrow accounts, failing which treaty benefits, the participation exemption, and favorable tax rulings can be denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful filing of false or incomplete tax returns; deliberate understatement of crowdfunding success fees; fabrication of deductible expenses; use of undisclosed foreign escrow accounts; diversion of portal income to a sham non-resident entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal imprisonment up to 5 years; criminal fine up to EUR 500,000 under the law of 25 March 2020; mandatory 10% evasion surcharge on the evaded taxes; default interest of 0.8% per month; revocation of all loss carryforwards and tax credits; automatic re-assessment for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations are criminally liable with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000; personal civil exposure to the fiscal authority for the full evaded amount plus interest; asset tracing and seizure of personal bank accounts; travel bans pending criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Arrangement, Shell Company and GAAR Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a letterbox SARL without employees, premises, or Luxembourg decision-making; circular financing arrangements to manufacture deductions; acquiring holding participations solely to exploit the participation exemption; structuring portfolio crowdfunding loans to strip taxable income to a zero-tax related entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization and denial of treaty and directive benefits under ATAD GAAR; disallowance of the participation exemption with reassessment at 24.94% combined rate; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; potential unilateral penalty increase of 10% on the additional assessment; EU Unshell Directive (ATAD 3) pending thresholds impose minimum substance reporting with fines and deemed-shareholder consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally assessed for unpaid taxes where the arrangement constitutes wrongful management under Article 710-1 of the Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915; courts pierce the veil upon proof of sham incorporation; managing directors face civil restitution to creditors and the tax administration; criminal conviction for use of fictitious corporate vehicles.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Crowdfunding Operation and AML/CFT Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the equity crowdfunding portal without the CSSF license under Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 (ECSPR) or the legacy Luxembourg law of 17 December 2018; failure to conduct CDD/KYC on retail investors; omission of suspicious transaction reports; failure to segregate escrowed investor funds; concealment of beneficial owners in the RBE register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for compliance breaches; criminal AML penalties of imprisonment from 5 to 10 years and fines up to EUR 5,000,000 under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, as amended; immediate license revocation and deletion from the ECSPR register; forfeiture of the crowdfunding business and freeze of all escrow accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers are personally prosecutable for personal knowledge of money laundering conduits; imprisonment up to 10 years and personal fines up to EUR 5,000,000; civil liability to defrauded retail investors for losses; professional disqualification and travel bans; personal seizure of management assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File, Late Filing and Non-Payment of Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the extended 31 December filing deadline; failure to pay assessed CIT, municipal business tax and net wealth tax instalments; deliberate non-submission of the RCS annual accounts; ignoring ACD reminders and formal summons; obstruction of tax audit requests.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late filing fines up to EUR 25,000; imposition d'office with burden of proof reversed against the taxpayer; default interest 0.8% per commenced month on the entire unpaid balance; additional 10% late-payment surcharge; forced collection through garnishment of the SARL's escrow and bank accounts; fines up to EUR 5,000 for annual accounts non-disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly fail to cause voluntary liquidation or filing may be held personally liable for the company's tax debts to the extent of mismanagement; courts may order civil restitution of dissipated funds; exit bans (interdiction de séjour) and passport retention are commonly issued for tax debts above threshold amounts; imprisonment in aggravated fraud scenarios.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misstatement and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of contemporaneous Local File documentation despite related-party transactions exceeding EUR 100,000; charging non-arm's length management fees to investor SPVs; allocating Luxembourg IT development value to a foreign affiliate without compensation; failing to benchmark the crowdfunding platform's margin under TNMM; retroactive and untimely documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty adjustments and primary TP adjustment with a 10% surcharge on undeclared profit; refusal of the corresponding deductions; default interest applied to the offset tax; denial of Master File/Local File acceptance leading to evidence-weight penalties; Luxembourg courts uphold ACD determinations when documentation is absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign tax returns without TP documentation expose themselves to fines up to EUR 25,000 for incomplete declarations; personal civil liability toward the state for the undervalued tax base where they knowingly approved the mispricing; criminal proceedings for false certificates in cross-border group documentation.
